Suppress small unweighted cells in a survey summary

Source: R/suppress.R
nis_suppress.Rd

Mask a summary using unweighted counts and contributing hospitals.

Usage

nis_suppress(
  .data,
  threshold = 10,
  ...,
  count_col,
  weighted_cols = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  secondary = TRUE,
  hospital_col = NULL
)

Arguments

.data

A gtsummary::tbl_svysummary() result, optionally with add_p() or add_overall(), or a data frame/tibble.

threshold

Maximum unweighted cell count to suppress.

...

Reserved for compatibility; unused arguments are errors.

count_col

<tidy-select> For data frames, select exactly one unweighted-count column.

weighted_cols

<tidy-select> For data frames, other columns to mask on primary and secondary rows.

by

<tidy-select> Optional data-frame grouping columns defining strata for complementary suppression.

secondary

Apply complementary suppression. For data frames this masks the smallest remaining positive count when exactly one row in a stratum is primary-masked. This is single-dimension complementary suppression, not a full cell-suppression solver; totals rows must be handled or excluded by the user.

hospital_col

<tidy-select> Optional selection of a single data-frame column containing the number of distinct contributing hospitals for each cell. Cells with fewer than two hospitals are marked <2 hospitals. Missing or invalid hospital counts are errors. Hospital identifiers must be counted by year; nis_cell_counts() computes counts from record-level data or an nis_design() result.

Value

For data frames, the same table with masked columns converted to character. For gtsummary results, the table with primary and secondary masks and a footnote describing them.

Details

In a survey table, each statistic is checked against its supporting discharges and hospital-years. The function stops when it cannot identify the records behind a statistic. It also checks the non-missing complement of a displayed two-level indicator and can mask related overall statistics. If one categorical level in a column is masked, the function also masks the smallest remaining positive level. Review other deductions from related outputs before release.

In a data frame, supply unweighted counts and, when available, distinct hospital counts. Grouped complementary suppression can mask an additional positive cell when there is one primary mask in a group. Review totals and any other cells that someone could recover by subtraction.

See also

Check disclosure before sharing results, Check disclosure before sharing results.

Other disclosure: nis_cell_counts()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")

design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, RACE))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
table <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = RACE,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE)
)
nis_suppress(table, threshold = 10)

Before sharing under the HCUP Data Use Agreement, review tables for other derivable cells.
